transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (CTO - Mossbridge), Samir Patel (Head of ML), Liam Wu (DevOps)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Jordan: Quick intro and agenda - time-to-first-token, credits, hosting fit.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:05] Dana (Mossbridge): Good, thanks. Busy week, but excited to talk through this.
[00:12] Samir: Hi, Samir here. We're evaluating options for customer support routing and a product search assistant, mostly as a rapid pilot to start.
[00:19] Jordan: Perfect. Quick agenda — 1) understand what you want to do and success criteria, 2) hosting options and security questions, 3) time-to-first-token — credits and starter repo, and 4) next steps. Sound OK?
[00:28] Liam: Yep. Also we want to understand what changes we need on infra side, like VPC peering or VPN.
[00:33] Priya (Redwood): Hi, I can cover the dev onboarding and pilot checklist. I'll also go through the basic benchmarks we recommend.
[01:02] Dana: High level — we are a mid-market retail platform, heavy traffic spikes during sale windows, most sensitive data is PII tied to orders. We want a POC in two weeks to validate latency and cost.
[01:18] Samir: Target is sub-250ms median for the product search endpoint at 95th percentile under our batch size, but it's flexible. Quality metrics: retrieval precision and answer hallucination rate — we have prompt sets.
[01:33] Jordan: Great. Couple clarifying q's — what does your current stack look like? Are you running embeddings index on-prem or in cloud?
[01:42] Samir: Embeddings in cloud (managed vector DB). Most infra in AWS us-east-1. We prefer not to egress PII out of region if possible.
[01:50] Jordan: Noted. On hosting, there are three main paths: Redwood Hosted API (fastest TTFT), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), and Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem for strict controls). Which of these seems close to what you're thinking?
[02:10] Dana: Ideally we want to start hosted for speed, but later we probably need VPC or private deployment for compliance reasons. Can you explain the timeline and cost tradeoffs?
[02:20] Priya: Sure — Hosted is basically: create account, we give you API keys and starter repo; you can be making your first calls in under an hour. We also provision free trial credits — you'll get a starter allotment (we discussed 30k tokens equiv earlier) to run prompt tests.
[02:34] Jordan: For Dedicated, it's a reserved capacity model — more predictable latency during spikes because you get a GPU pool allocated to you. That requires a commit and typically a 30–90 day ramp. Private (VPC) has the most isolation; we connect to your VPC via VPC peering or private link and you manage KMS. That takes more time — typically 2–6 weeks depending on approvals.
[02:54] Liam: For VPC, do we need to open any inbound ports? How's the control plane managed?
[03:01] Priya: No inbound ports for your infra; we use outbound TLS to our private ingress. Control plane is optional — for Private deployments you'll host a control plane in your VPC or we can run it with private endpoints. KMS integration works with customer-managed keys; we can accept HSM-backed KMS.
[03:18] Dana: SOC2 — do you have docs? We will need info for procurement.
[03:23] Jordan: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and our latest pen-test summary. We'll also send a network diagram and KMS integration notes.
[03:29] Samir: Regarding latency, you mentioned caching — how transparent is prefix or KV cache? We do conversational search where users often have follow-ups.
[03:36] Priya: We support automatic KV/prefix caching; it helps with long-running conversations and reduces token spend. Note: when you use extremely long context windows the caching hit rate drops, obviously. Also structure your prompts to leverage caching — separate instructions from user content.
[03:50] Jordan: Also, for cost reduction, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization or model variants per route. For a pilot we usually test an unquantized higher-accuracy model then try a quantized variant for steady state.
[04:04] Dana: How are model rollouts handled? If we pin a model version, can Redwood roll forward safely in case of regression?
[04:09] Priya: Yes. We have rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a previous model variant. And you can pin per-route. Rollbacks are instant if the variant is compatible.
[04:19] Liam: What about data residency? If we run hosted in us-east-1 but some customers are EU, can we shard by region?
[04:25] Jordan: Smart routing can route by region or tenancy. We can provision hosted instances in EU regions or recommend Dedicated/Private if EU residency is required.
[04:34] Samir: On authentication—SSO support and RBAC?
[04:37] Priya: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, and token-level RBAC. Audit logs can be forwarded via syslog or copied to your SIEM.
[04:46] Jordan: Ok, quick qualification on scale — what's expected qps during pilot vs production?
[04:50] Dana: Pilot should be a few hundred qps at most, production target is low thousands during sale peaks. That's why we're nervous about latency spikes.
[04:58] Jordan: For predictable peaks, Dedicated is the safest from a throughput angle but has commit costs. We can mock the sale scenario in a benchmark.
[05:05] Priya: I'll design a benchmark that simulates your peak profile. We'll include cold vs warm cache runs, and a long conversation follow-up pattern to check KV cache effectiveness.
[05:15] Samir: Sounds good. For the free credits, what's the typical amount for this type of POC? You mentioned 30k earlier — enough?
[05:22] Jordan: We typically provide an initial 30k tokens-equivalent credit for PLG trials; for a dedicated pilot we can extend that or provide a focused pilot credit bucket. We'll confirm in the follow-up email.
[05:31] Dana: How do we onboard engineers? Any SDKs?
[05:33] Priya: We have REST and SDKs (Python/Node/Go). Starter repo includes quickstart, sample prompts, recommended batching settings, and a scripts folder for running perf tests. Time-to-first-token for a developer who follows the repo is usually < 1 hour.
[05:45] Liam: For infra changes — if we go VPC, what's the typical network setup and CI/CD implications?
[05:50] Priya: Typical options are VPC peering or PrivateLink; you'll want a dedicated subnet and security groups that allow outbound to our endpoints. CI/CD wise, you'll add secrets to your pipeline referencing the customer-managed KMS. We provide templates for Terraform and CloudFormation.
[06:06] Jordan: Any blockers on compliance side?
[06:08] Dana: We need to check legal on subprocessor lists and the DPA. Also our security team wants KMS keys stored in our HSM.
[06:15] Jordan: We can share the subprocessor list and DPA template. HSM-backed KMS is supported for Private deployments.
[06:22] Samir: On the model side — do you recommend using your curated open models or bring our own? We have a fine-tuned family for product descriptions internally.
[06:29] Priya: You can bring-your-own model artifact or use one of the curated open models in our catalog. For POCs we often start with a well-tested open model and then evaluate BYOM for tighter quality. Note: BYOM on Dedicated/Private has slightly more onboarding steps.
[06:43] Liam: Is there a limit to how large a model we can attach to Dedicated pools?
[06:46] Priya: It depends on GPU type; our team will size the pool. If you're using large context models, we usually suggest a multi-GPU setup or sequence-length optimizations.
[06:55] Jordan: Quick check — what would success look like for this pilot in two weeks?
[06:59] Samir: Verified 95th percentile latency < 300ms for core search traffic, and acceptable cost per seat — we have a cost target. Also low hallucination rate on our prompt tests.
[07:10] Dana: And legal sign-off to proceed to Dedicated if the pilot is successful.
[07:14] Jordan: OK, so proposed next steps: 1) we provision the starter credits and repo; 2) Priya and Samir run the perf plan and exchange traffic profiles; 3) we'll schedule a benchmark run and review session at the end of the week. Anything else?
[07:28] Samir: Can Priya also include the exact metrics we'll capture? Like p50/p95/p99, cache hit rate, token breakdown?
[07:36] Priya: Yes — I'll share a perf checklist with the metrics and scripts.
[07:41] Dana: Please send the security pack to procurement (procurement@mossbridge.com).
[07:44] Jordan: Will do. We'll email the SOC2, DPA template, and the network diagram.
[07:49] Liam: Quick question — what happens if during pilot we see a regression after a model rollout? How fast is rollback?
[07:55] Priya: Rollbacks are immediate to pinned variant if compatible. We also support traffic mirroring for canary tests so you can evaluate without exposing to end users.
[08:05] Samir: Ok great. Do you have any suggestions for prompt design to minimize hallucinations?
[08:09] Priya: Several — keep instructions separate, include grounding context with retrieval, apply temperature controls, and use reranking for top-k candidates. We'll include examples in the starter repo.
[08:22] Jordan: Alright, wrapping up — recap of next steps I will send an email with credits and the starter repo link, Priya will send the perf plan and benchmarks, we'll plan a 1-week pilot starting week of 6/14, and procurement will get the security pack.
[08:40] Dana: Thanks everyone, that's clear.
[08:43] Jordan: Thanks for your time. We'll follow up within 24 hours.
